stories.notes: Story has no acceptance criteria and involves live preview across multiple platforms (GO, UP, MX) in a CMS — a complex, real-time content rendering feature. openspec should elaborate requirements and define AC first; speckit should then harden with testability criteria, security checks, and edge cases for cross-platform preview rendering.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new capability (Live Preview of Content in CMS) that does not exist in the codebase. useContent is the central attachment point — it funnels content to 236+ consumers via getContentByKey(). Any live-preview mechanism must plug in there to propagate draft content to all consuming components without individual changes. No fix site exists; this is novel work. VCs derived entirely from the description since ACs are empty. VCs stop at our side of the Contentstack API boundary.

Openspec provided an empty AC list with valuable architectural context: useContent is the central funnel reaching 236+ consumers via getContentByKey(), and any live-preview mechanism must plug in there. I built the full AC set from scratch based on the story title, file paths, and openspec's notes. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1 ensures the core architectural goal — all consumers get draft content through the existing funnel with zero per-component changes. (2) AC-2 covers real-time updates, the defining feature of live preview. (3) AC-3 covers session exit. (4) AC-4/AC-11 cover visual and accessible indication of preview mode. (5) AC-5/AC-6 cover error and fallback paths — connection loss and API errors. (6) AC-7 covers rapid-update race conditions. (7) AC-8 covers route navigation persistence. (8) AC-9 covers security — only valid params activate preview. (9) AC-10 ensures zero overhead for non-preview users. (10) AC-12 covers the edge case where a draft doesn't exist for a given key. CAVEAT: File contents were unavailable during this review. The criteria are derived from the story title, file paths, and openspec's architectural notes. Some criteria may need adjustment once the actual implementation of useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, and contentstack.ts is examined — for example, the exact mechanism by which preview parameters enter the app (URL query string vs. other) and the Contentstack SDK's live-preview API contract may refine AC-1 and AC-9.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec provided critical architectural context (useContent as central funnel reaching 236+ consumers via getContentByKey, novel work with no fix site), while speckit built a comprehensive 12-AC set from scratch covering real-time updates, error/fallback paths, security, accessibility, race conditions, and zero-overhead guarantees. However, speckit explicitly noted file contents were unavailable during review and that criteria were derived from title, file paths, and openspec notes only. This introduces risk that ACs may need adjustment once actual implementations of useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, and contentstack.ts are examined — particularly AC-1 (preview parameter entry mechanism) and AC-9 (Contentstack SDK live-preview API contract). Human review recommended to validate ACs against actual codebase before implementation.
